Other Music Game Appearances: * [[AC DDR 2014|DanceDanceRevolution (2014)]] == Lyrics == None. == Song Connections / Remixes == * MAX.(period) is a remix of [[MAX 300]], from [[AC DDRMAX|DDRMAX -DanceDanceRevolution 6thMIX-]]. * MAX.(period) samples [[PARANOiA]] in the middle of the song. * MAX.(period) was performed live as part of the ''DanceDanceRevolution 20th Anniversary NONSTOP MEGAMIX'' medley at [[KONAMI Arcade Championship|The 7th KONAMI Arcade Championship]]. == Trivia == {{Gallery}} * MAX.(period)'s banner appears unused in the [[AC DDR SuperNOVA|DanceDanceRevolution SuperNOVA]] data. * MAX.(period) appears in DanceDanceRevolution (2014) as the ENCORE EXTRA STAGE song of the ''Replicant D-ignition'' event, achieved by obtaining a AA or greater on [[EGOISM 440]]. The RISKY, REVERSE, and 1.5x Hi-SPEED modifiers were forced when playing the song. Clearing it would unlock "[[RINON|The Dark One]]" as a selectable dancer. ** As of Replicant D-ignition's 2nd Phase, MAX.(period) was moved down to EXTRA STAGE, but could still be accessed as an ENCORE EXTRA STAGE by obtaining a AA or greater on EGOISM 440. By obtaining a AA or greater on MAX.(period) as the EXTRA STAGE would immediately trigger [[Over The "Period"|Over The “Period”]] as the ENCORE EXTRA STAGE and unlock RINON as a selectable dancer. *** MAX.(period)'s CHALLENGE charts are available as of Replicant D-ignition's 2nd Phase, as well. ** From August 6th to December 23rd, 2015, MAX.(period) could be unlocked via the ''EXTRA ATTACK'' unlocking system, after unlocking EGOISM 440. Note that the SURVIVED BONUS meter had to be filled on BEGINNER, then BASIC, DIFFICULT, and then finally EXPERT. *** MAX.(period)'s CHALLENGE charts could be unlocked via EXTRA ATTACK after unlocking Over The “Period”'s EXPERT charts. ** From December 24th, 2015 onwards, MAX.(period) has been automatically unlocked for all players. * MAX.(period) received new CHALLENGE charts in the arcade DanceDanceRevolution titles, replacing its old ones. ** This was previously hinted by Yuichi Asami during an autograph session on July 7th, 2012, where when asked if it was time to port MAX.(period) to arcades, he replied "That's what I think, too. Recently, the difficulty level is increasing. If it was ported, it would be even harder." [https://twitter.com/NICEBaal/status/221604786036940802]. * During the 180 BPM section of the song, MAX.(period)'s charts (except for BEGINNER) use portions of PARANOiA's charts. ** MAX.(period)'s new CHALLENGE charts use parts of PARANOiA (X-Special)'s charts. ** Coincidentally, if one were to play PARANOiA and MAX.(period) at the same time, they'll both synchronize at said portion [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6WlVxGvu3v4]. * In MAX.(period)'s video, a video clip of PARANOiA being selected and played on [[CS DDR 1st JP|DanceDanceRevolution CS (Japan)]] is shown. * MAX.(period)'s jacket and new background image in the video feature the Wii dance mat, instead of the PlayStation / PlayStation 2 dance mat used in its original background and banner. ** MAX.(period)'s video is also now played in the background of a dark blue-recolored version of the REPLICANT background dance stage and is not full-screen prior to [[AC DDR WORLD|DanceDanceRevolution WORLD]]. * When MAX.(period) is played and cleared as an ENCORE EXTRA STAGE, the "CLEARED" shutter is delayed by about nine seconds (compared to when played on any other stage), to synchronize it with the sound effect of the shutter in the song. ** This delay is present from [[AC DDR A|DanceDanceRevolution A]] onwards, regardless of the stage MAX.(period) is played on. The delay also caused all of MAX.(period)'s charts to have their [[GROOVE RADAR]] values slightly lowered due to the song's gameplay length increasing. * MAX.(period) ranked #1 in the BEMANI Fan Site CHECK!SONGS Monthly Ranking list for May 2015. * MAX.(period)'s difficulty level change from [[AC DDR A20|DanceDanceRevolution A20]] was applied to DanceDanceRevolution A on March 27th, 2019. * MAX.(period) is available in [[CS DDR GRAND PRIX|DanceDanceRevolution GRAND PRIX]]'s GRAND PRIX mode from May 8th, 2024, by purchasing '''GRAND PRIX music pack vol.26''' (グランプリ楽曲パック vol.26). * Prior to DanceDanceRevolution WORLD, MAX.(period)'s BPM was shown as 150-600 for all of its difficulties. == Song Production Information == === 2MB ===

Note that you required a PERFECT FULL COMBO on Over The “Period”'s charts in order to clear it. ** This marks the second time a PERFECT FULL COMBO is required to clear the ENCORE EXTRA STAGE, after [[LOVE IS THE POWER -Re:born-]] in [[AC DDR X3|DanceDanceRevolution X3 VS 2ndMIX]]. *** Currently, LOVE IS THE POWER -Re:born-, Over The “Period”, and [[ACE FOR ACES]] are the only songs in the DanceDanceRevolution series that required a PERFECT FULL COMBO to complete (as ENCORE EXTRA STAGE songs). ** As of April 9th, 2015, obtaining a AA or greater on MAX.(period)'s EXPERT chart allowed access to Over The “Period”'s BASIC chart as the ENCORE EXTRA STAGE. ** As of May 1st, 2015, obtaining a AA or greater on MAX.(period)'s DIFFICULT chart allowed access to Over The “Period”'s BEGINNER chart as the ENCORE EXTRA STAGE (BASIC if on Double Play). ** As of July 2nd, 2015, obtaining a AA or greater on MAX.(period)'s BASIC chart also allowed access to Over The “Period”'s BEGINNER chart as the ENCORE EXTRA STAGE (BASIC if on Double Play). ** From August 6th to December 23rd, 2015, Over The “Period” could be unlocked via the ''EXTRA ATTACK'' unlocking system, after unlocking MAX.(period). Note that the SURVIVED BONUS meter had to be filled on BEGINNER, then BASIC, DIFFICULT, and then finally EXPERT. ** From December 24th, 2015 onwards, Over The “Period” has been automatically unlocked for all players. *** It also received CHALLENGE charts on December 24th, 2015. These charts were exclusive to EXTRA STAGE, and could not be unlocked via-EXTRA ATTACK. **** From DanceDanceRevolution A onwards, Over The “Period”'s CHALLENGE charts are playable by default. * Over The “Period” is one of two songs in DanceDanceRevolution (2014) to have CHALLENGE charts rated Level 19, with the other being [[EGOISM 440]]. ** Its Single CHALLENGE and Double CHALLENGE charts are DanceDanceRevolution WORLD, and in DanceDanceRevolution GRAND PRIX, Over The “Period”'s BPM is displayed as 23-840. * In DanceDanceRevolution GRAND PRIX, Over The “Period” received its difficulty changes from DanceDanceRevolution WORLD on July 3rd, 2024. == Song Production Information == === TAG === I had planned the story for Replicant D-ignition from the beginning. First of all, MAX.(period) was going to be included in the arcade version.
MAX.(period) was recorded in [[CS DDR EXTREME JP|the game that was the counterpart]] of the [[AC DDR EXTREME|rumored final arcade title]], I myself knew this so I was hesitant to record.
But I was against it. Pretending to end. It is not going to end. Is it just dramatic? Replicant D-ignition began.
It was finished with EGOISM 440, a really good job by [[Yuichi Asami|U1]], and then MAX.(period) appearing at full force. Is the arcade series finally over? How many people thought it was?
Meanwhile, someone tweeted. "TAG has yet to appear" It was a very good read.
This song appeared in Phase 2 after a short period, and the excitement when this song appeared was extraordinary, to the point where some knees trembled. So the condition was clearing the ENCORE EXTRA STAGE with a PERFECT FULL COMBO while playing in DIFFICULT? Now that Good is part of a combo, it seemed like that antithesis of hard.
I think that there was not a sense of tension at all. Since X3's LOVE IS THE POWER was cleared up easily, this time the Difficult chart was made Level 15 so it would not be able to be cleared that easily, but it was a bit overkill... It just rolled out in a direction that I never thought.
Top players recorded it. A song that was gradually cleared.
When the strategy battle involving not only Japan but Taiwan, South Korea, North America, etc. started, there was a feeling of excitement and expectation similar to whether human beings could reach an unknown planet for the first time.
I checked the progress everyday and was amazing. Today, the human race has reached so far. And when the long-awaited first clear arrived, I was happy as if I cleared it.
However, at that time there was another chart cleared besides Difficult. "Beginner chart seems to have been cleared... Even though it is the easiest chart of Over The “Period”", "It is a real hell...", but I knew the veteran player who came this far would do it. When the melody from Another Phase appears in the middle of the song, please remember the story that began with Another Phase, the song that symbolized the [[AC DDR 2013|DanceDanceRevolution title which removed the numbering]], and that ends with Over The “Period” (but it is not the end!).
Let's advance together. The light points to the place beyond. Why do you need KONAMI ORIGINAL songs?
Because...
== Jacket Design Information == === mayo === The direction was decided, it was a two-shot jacket featuring RINON and "The Dark One", it's an impressive jacket which I memorably remember drawing it while listening to TAG, [[Nagisa Nakamoto|NAGI]], and others in the staff team discussing about the story and the content of the event. Looking back to my work folder at the time, there are many patterns of rough layout images in which various words were written. I drew the jacket from one of the designs chosen by TAG chose from those layout images.
Among those words, one of the impressive words that were featured on it was "it's not a confrontation between those two characters".
While listening to the song, its jacket pictures the image of what is further beyond the end. == Difficulty & Notecounts == DanceDanceRevolution difficulty rated from 1 to 20 from X onwards. To unlock it, you must EX-HARD Clear [[Thor's Hammer]] with a AAA rank to access this song. ** As of November 7th, 2012, Plan 8 is accessed by clearing Thor's Hammer with any type of gauge, under specific rank conditions depending on the difficulty chosen. All the charts are accessible. ** In [[AC SPADA|beatmania IIDX 21 SPADA]], its NORMAL, HYPER, and ANOTHER charts can be unlocked by obtaining 52, 60, and 68 Tran Medals respectively. ** As of December 19th, 2013, it is unlocked by default. * When Plan 8 is played as a boss stage in LEGEND CROSS, the arcade LED ticker displays "RED BOSS 12". * Plan 8 is Ryu☆'s first ONE MORE EXTRA STAGE song since [[3y3s]] in [[AC EMPRESS|beatmania IIDX 16 EMPRESS]]. * The boss in Plan 8's overlays is ''Red Ripika'', one of the joker villains in the story of beatmania IIDX 20 tricoro. ** In the first half of the song, the boss appears as a chibi character like in the LEGEND CROSS cutscenes. Only in this form, its animations are played regardless of the player's performance. ** In the second half of the song, the boss evolves to its second, "magic blade" form. It appears as a huge, red mech which is based on the chibi version. The red ''Boss Crystals'' float around it. If the boss is not attacking or taking damage, the bright shield that envelopes it becomes temporarily visible. *** When you miss a note, the real form of Red Ripika comes out from the mech and attacks the Q-pro avatar with the Boss Crystals. ** In the last cutscene of LEGEND CROSS, Red Ripika retreats. * The name Plan 8 was used by Ryu☆'s unit with a friend back when he was a student in high school in 1997. (1997 is also the year he started to write music.) ** He notes in the song production information for Plan 8 that the name itself comes from the Ed Wood movie ''Plan 9 from Outer Space''. * Plan 8 could be unlocked from February 27th, 2013 to March 3rd, 2014 in jubeat saucer as part of the [[Cafe de Tran|Café de Tran]] unlock system. It was the sixth unlockable song for that game. ** In [[AC jb saucer fulfill|jubeat saucer fulfill]], it can be unlocked as part of ''saucer macchiato'''s Side Menu from May 1st, 2014. ** In [[AC jb prop|jubeat prop]], it can be unlocked by playing it as a BONUS TUNE from May 28th, 2015. ** In [[AC jb Qubell|jubeat Qubell]], it is one of the Garnet unlocks of the ''dig dig Qubell'' unlocking system. ** In [[AC jb clan|jubeat clan]], it can be unlocked in the ''jubeat SHOP''. ** In [[AC jb festo|jubeat festo]], it can be purchased at the ''emo MART''. ** In [[AC jb Ave.|jubeat Ave.]] and [[AC jb beyond the Ave.|beyond the Ave.]], it is one of the CONCIERGE unlocks of the ''LIGHT CHAT'' unlocking system from August 17th, 2022. * In the U.S./EU iTunes version of the ''beatmania IIDX 20 tricoro ORIGINAL SOUNDTRACK Vol.1'' album, the star on the artist is omitted. * Plan 8 could be unlocked in DanceDanceRevolution (2014) from January 22nd, 2015 as part of the ''BOSS ON PARADE'' event. ** To access Plan 8, you had to play any song in the beatmania IIDX folder (when sorting songs under BEMANI Series (BEMANIシリーズから選ぶ)) whose genre features the word "HAPPY" in it. For a complete list of supported songs, please see [[BOSS ON PARADE Medal-supported Songs|this page]]. ** From December 24th, 2015 onwards, Plan 8 has been automatically unlocked for all players. * Plan 8 is available in [[CS INFINITAS|beatmania IIDX INFINITAS]] by purchasing '''beatmania IIDX INFINITAS Music Pack vol.4''' (beatmania IIDX INFINITAS 楽曲パック vol.4). * Plan 8's [[CS jb 2021|jubeat (2021)]] ratings were adjusted to its jubeat festo ratings on March 7th, 2022. * Plan 8 is available in [[CS DDR GRAND PRIX|DanceDanceRevolution GRAND PRIX]]'s GRAND PRIX mode from March 13th, 2024, by purchasing '''BEMANI SELECTION music pack vol.1''' (BEMANI SELECTION楽曲パック vol.1). ** It received brand-new CHALLENGE charts. By purchasing the pack with an active subscription, Plan 8's CHALLENGE charts can be played in [[AC DDR A3|DanceDanceRevolution A3]] and [[AC DDR WORLD|DanceDanceRevolution WORLD]]. ** From March 31st, 2025 in DanceDanceRevolution WORLD, these charts are available by default for all players. * Plan 8 is available in SOUND VOLTEX EXCEED GEAR コナステ from March 13th, 2025, by purchasing '''Konasute SOUND VOLTEX BEMANI Selection Music Pack vol.3''' (コナステ版 SOUND VOLTEX BEMANI セレクション 楽曲パック vol.3). * Plan 8 was added to SOUND VOLTEX ∇ on January 15th, 2026. == Song Production Information == === Ryu☆ === First of all, congratulations on BEMANI's 15th anniversary and beatmania IIDX 20's release!
I'm truly honored to have been in charge of the boss track for such a commemorative title.
This song was created around the theme of 1997, the year the [[AC bm 1st|original beatmania]] was born. The title, Plan 8, comes from a music production unit I formed with a friend back in 1997, also called Plan 8.
The main melody in the latter half was also taken from a song we made at that time, "Theme of Plan 8".
(Incidentally, the unit name comes from the legendary film "Plan 9 from Outer Space".) As for the genre "HAPPY GABBA", it does indeed exist.
In Plan 8, I included not only "HAPPY GABBA", but also root elements leading to "HAPPY HARDCORE", such as "OLD SKOOL" and "PIANO BREAKBEATS", all of which I had been intensely into back in 1997, arranged to fit the game. It has been 15 years since beatmania was born, and I can only admire the simple yet profound game system that has continued to entertain everyone without changing at all.
As someone who has been a beatmania fan for 15 years, I'll continue to devote myself to make more content so everyone can enjoy it even a little more. == Video Production Information == === GOLI === The first RED event "LEGEND CROSS" features the final boss song. I wondered what kind of song it would be, and it turned out to be an incredibly high-tension, insanely difficult track.
I was busy with other work, like tricoro's STEP UP Q-Pro and so on, so squeezing in time to make this was tough... The first half feels like a boss battle, focusing on red Repika vs. Q-Pro, while the second half unleashes her true potential with Repika's attack after she transforms.
Don't think of the bulky form as a powered suit. Imagine it more like a magical girl's sparkling transformation.

Its SPECIAL chart could be purchased for 8 VOLZZA KEYs after clearing the song. ** In [[AC RB VOLZZA 2|REFLEC BEAT VOLZZA 2]], it was playable by default. * starmine received a different set of jackets in the REFLEC BEAT series. * starmine was available in [[CS INFINITAS|beatmania IIDX INFINITAS]]' championship Mode from March 9th to 21st, 2016. ** On March 22nd, 2016, it was added to standard Mode for anyone who had played the [[Ryu BEST -STARLiGHT-|STARLiGHT CUP]] in championship Mode at least once. ** From December 2019, it can be purchased with BITs. * After being removed from the initial release of [[AC RB Reflesia|REFLEC BEAT 悠久のリフレシア]], starmine was revived on March 12th, 2020. * starmine is available in DanceDanceRevolution GRAND PRIX's GRAND PRIX mode from May 25th, 2023, by purchasing '''GRAND PRIX music pack vol.21''' (グランプリ楽曲パック vol.21). ** It received brand-new CHALLENGE charts, which become available by purchasing both this and '''GRAND PRIX music pack vol.22''' (グランプリ楽曲パック vol.22). ** By purchasing both packs with an active subscription, starmine's CHALLENGE charts can be played in [[AC DDR A3|DanceDanceRevolution A3]]. ** From May 31st, 2024 in DanceDanceRevolution A3, they are available by default for all players. == Song Production Information == === beatmania IIDX === ==== Ryu ==== Ryu here.
Actually, I made this song back when I was in high school, so it's a pretty old song.
So I had to remake it for this IIDX song contest. What do you think about it?
It's a Happy song, so it's easy to get used to, but the BPM is 182 which is... too fast... I think I'll play it in LIGHT7 mode myself. Hehe.
Finally, I would like to thank dj TAKA, [[Tomoyuki Uchida|Ucchie]], and all the staff members for their hard work in this project, and for listening to my unreasonable and selfish requests.
It was a very good experience. Thank you very much. === REFLEC BEAT === ==== kors k ==== The [[AC 3rd style|IIDX 3rd style]] music contest was a huge turning point for my life. I remember running to the arcade on IIDX 4th style's release date to find out what kind of song the other selected person create!? It's a super pop, cute, and great song! == Video Production Information == === VJ GYO === Thanks to your support, this song has been a big hit after the release of IIDX 4th. It's composed by Ryu, a university student from Fukuoka.
It's a cheerful, dazzling, pleasant song which directly matches dj TAKA's thoughts on the word "HAPPY", which is the direction of 4th style. I think it was right around the time of IIDX 4th when Ryu was approached to work on the game version of his song.
The entire team was in a desperate situation, and I also didn't have time to decide what to do with the movie, so I just started to add ideas like an association game: starmine→repeated fireworks→yukata→uchiwa→bon odori...
And then...
Footage of fireworks?→materials recorded from the previous year (I'm sad it was from last year). What about the bon odori?→live-action wasn't ready on time (I'm hesitant to make it with the staff)→CG→an easily moveable character→TRAN... That's the background sequence of events.
And then...
We were in such a hurry that it ended being quite rushed, and I couldn't capture the song's splendor... There are many things about this process which I regret. Moreover, I ended the theory that TRAN was only in trance songs, which changed from her previously serious mood to having fun (She's expressionless but somehow looks like this... I think). I'm relieved that fans seem to receive her dancing very favorably. == Difficulty & Notecounts == beatmania IIDX to 10th style difficulty rated from 1 to 7 in 4th style, 1 to 7+ from 5th through 9th style, 1 to 8 in 10th style, 1 to 8+ in IIDX RED, and 1 to 12 from HAPPY SKY onwards.

However, it is not extended. * In pop'n music, instead of displaying its character's portrait, Thank You Merry Christmas displays its jacket in the song selection screen. ** Unlike other default KONAMI originals, Thank You Merry Christmas' EX chart was unlocked by default in pop'n music éclale. * Thank You Merry Christmas is available in [[CS DDR GRAND PRIX|DanceDanceRevolution GRAND PRIX]]'s GRAND PRIX mode from December 21st, 2023, by purchasing '''GRAND PRIX music pack vol.24''' (グランプリ楽曲パック vol.24). ** It received brand-new CHALLENGE charts, which become available by purchasing both this and '''GRAND PRIX music pack vol.23''' (グランプリ楽曲パック vol.23). ** By purchasing both packs with an active subscription, Thank You Merry Christmas' CHALLENGE charts can be played in [[AC DDR A3|DanceDanceRevolution A3]] and [[AC DDR WORLD|DanceDanceRevolution WORLD]]. ** From December 27th, 2024 in DanceDanceRevolution WORLD, these charts are available by default for all players. * Thank You Merry Christmas is available in [[CS pnm Lively|pop'n music Lively]] by purchasing '''pop'n music Lively Music Pack vol.15''' (pop'n music Lively 楽曲パック vol.15). == Music Comment == None. == Song Production Information == Untranslated. == Jacket Design Information == === isonin === I was seriously embarrassed by the "kimi wo aishite iru kara~" part. I'm isonin. The REFLEC, DDR, jubeat characters, and the VENUS duo are having a Christmas party!
I want to immediately jump into this gentle world right now. I wonder what I'd be like... like a little match girl...
It's like peeking into a party from the window outside... that's what I had in mind while drawing it.
This warm yet sad and distinct atmosphere, is unique to Christmas. I received the jacket image in advance, so while I was wondering what kind of song it'd become~, I was earnestly listening to a Christmas music box medley that I appropriately found. When drawing jackets, I generally listen to the song on the jacket while wearing earphones, but this time, the jacket and song were simultaneously progressing smoothly, so I drew it while feeling uplifted by the music box medley.
I found out that I'm moved by music boxes. They make me cry.
The difference between listening to it with and without earphones is amazing, as if I'm just in another world. I never dreamed that the person sitting next to me was somehow frowning while listening to such pure music.
Yes, I went into another world. For the jacket image, I first received quite a specific order, so afterwards, when I wondered if I had enough time to summarize it well and tightly with a cute feeling~, the checked pattern in the background was quite difficult, and I thought to myself, "checked craftsmen are amazing!".
I don't know if such craftsmen exist. This jacket is packed with as many characters from each BEMANI game series as possible.
They're getting excited everywhere, so if you look very closely, I think you'll have brand-new discoveries!
Have a great Merry Christmas everyone~ Thank You Merry VENUS! == Character Information == None. == Difficulty & Notecounts == DanceDanceRevolution difficulty rated from 1 to 20 from X onwards.

But the base line or phrase that came to my mind was kind of funky and American. So I built on the momentum and created this very American song!
I hadn't been creating a mid tempo tune for a long time, so I had so much fun creating this song. === DanceDanceRevolution Community === This is a darker, yet high energy, song from the mind of DJ YOSHITAKA. He teams up with Robert "RAab" Stevenson, whose voice propels this song to the next level. RAab is an industry veteran, having worked with everyone from The Black Eyed Peas to Al Green. }} == Song Connections / Remixes == * An extended version of 爆なな☆てすとロイヤー appears in Nanahira's first best-of album, [[Confetti-Box]], and in the [[IOSYS RHYTHMICAL WORKS PERFECT HITS]] album. * The lyric "皇帝アイスクリーム" (koutei ice cream) in 爆なな☆てすとロイヤー may refer to [[Second Heaven]]'s "Somebody scream!" sample, which is an [[Inside Jokes#Somebody scream!|inside joke of the Japanese BEMANI community]]. * A sequel to 爆なな☆てすとロイヤー, titled [[Bakuzeni gatten worker|爆ゼニ☆がってんワーカー]], appears in [[AC Rootage|beatmania IIDX 26 Rootage]]. == Trivia == {{Gallery}} * 爆なな☆てすとロイヤー was added to BeatStream on March 19th, 2015. * 爆なな☆てすとロイヤー marks Youhei Kimura's first original composition in the BeatStream series. ** It also marks Nanahira's first and only original song in the BeatStream series. * Not counting the alternate cut of [[Totsugeki! Glass no kneeso hime!|突撃！ガラスのニーソ姫！]]'s video, 爆なな☆てすとロイヤー is the first KONAMI original Youhei Kimura song in BEMANI with its own unique video. * 爆なな☆てすとロイヤー received a NIGHTMARE chart in BeatStream on March 26th, 2015, unlockable via ''BEAST HACKER''. * 爆なな☆てすとロイヤー is one of the unlocks of the [[Kaitou BisCo no yokokujou!!]] (怪盗BisCoの予告状!!) event. It could be unlocked from June 17th to December 21st, 2015. ** In DanceDanceRevolution (2014), it is one of the panel unlocks of the DanceDanceRevolution Museum. *** From January 7th, 2016, 爆なな☆てすとロイヤー can be unlocked in DanceDanceRevolution (2014) via ''EXTRA ATTACK''. *** In [[AC DDR A|DanceDanceRevolution A]], 爆なな☆てすとロイヤー can be unlocked via ''EXTRA SAVIOR''. *** As of [[AC DDR A20|DanceDanceRevolution A20]], it is available by default. ** In REFLEC BEAT groovin'!! Upper, it is one of the panel unlocks of the REFLEC BEAT groovin'!! Upper Museum. *** In [[AC RB VOLZZA 2|REFLEC BEAT VOLZZA 2]], 爆なな☆てすとロイヤー could be purchased in the Garage for 20 VOLZZA KEYs. * Prior to [[AC DDR WORLD|DanceDanceRevolution WORLD]], 爆なな☆てすとロイヤー's music video eliminates any on-screen dancers. * The crossover of 爆なな☆てすとロイヤー to DanceDanceRevolution marks Nanahira's first appearance in that series. * In REFLEC BEAT, 爆なな☆てすとロイヤー uses its BeatStream LIGHT, MEDIUM, and BEAST jackets for its BASIC, MEDIUM, and HARD jackets, respectively. ** 爆なな☆てすとロイヤー's BeatStream BEAST jacket is used as the DanceDanceRevolution, jubeat, and ポラリスコード series' jacket. ** Also in SOUND VOLTEX, 爆なな☆てすとロイヤー uses its BeatStream LIGHT, MEDIUM, and BEAST jackets for its NOVICE, ADVANCED, and EXHAUST jackets, respectively. * HIGH TENSION was added to 爆なな☆てすとロイヤー's charts in [[AC BST AnimTribe|BeatStream アニムトライヴ]]. * 爆なな☆てすとロイヤー's BEAST chart was re-rated in BeatStream アニムトライヴ on January 13th, 2016. * 爆なな☆てすとロイヤー is a song part of the [[POLICY BREAK]] event. For more information on the dates it could be unlocked in the SOUND VOLTEX series, please see the event page. ** From January 18th, 2018 in [[AC SDVX IV|SOUND VOLTEX IV HEAVENLY HAVEN]], it can be purchased with BLOCKs instead. * 爆なな☆てすとロイヤー is automatically unlocked in jubeat Qubell from February 23rd, 2017 by having played BeatStream アニムトライヴ before February 13th, 2017, as part of Phase 1 of the ''BeatStream no ano kyokutachi ga jubeat demo asobechau!'' A smile that can be seen because of strong bonds. When they all passed around chocolates for Valentine's Day and ate them.
Marika Yamagata saw everyone getting along and laughing together with chocolate on their mouths, thought of the phrase "chocolate smile", and based on that, she improvised on the piano and created this song.
This is the first time that all the Hinatabi Bitter Sweets♪ members and the Coconatsu duo sang together, and it's the proud ending song of Season 3, with the theme of strong bonds. == Video Production Information == === VJ GYO with centralVillage === A choreography and dance for Hinatabi Bitter Sweets♪ & Coconatsu... As a present for such a special day, you can enjoy various flavors one at a time, with a movie that looks like an assortment of chocolates lined up like jewels!... We tried to make it like that. We'd be happy if you like it. == Character Information == None. == Choreography Information == === Natsumi Adachi === When you try your best at anything you like, there'll be a scene you can only see!

Other Music Game Appearances: * ミライダガッキ FutureTomTom Ver.2 == Lyrics == None yet. == Song Connections / Remixes == None. == Trivia == * ちゅ～いん☆バニー is one of the unlockable songs of DanceDanceRevolution (2014)'s ''EXTRA ATTACK'' unlocking system. It was added on June 5th, 2014. ** From December 17th, 2015 onwards, ちゅ～いん☆バニー has been automatically unlocked for all players. * ちゅ～いん☆バニー marks Yasuhiro Abe's first appearance in the DanceDanceRevolution series since [[AC DDR SuperNOVA2|DanceDanceRevolution SuperNOVA2]]'s [[dream of love]] and [[volcano]]. * ちゅ～いん☆バニー was first listed on the JASRAC database for around ''one year'' before it finally appeared as a playable song. ** It was also mentioned as a [[AC DDR 2013|DanceDanceRevolution (2013)]] song in [http://puretonemusic.jp/artist/miya/ Miyako Hagiwara's profile]. This was later removed. ** Unused data of ちゅ～いん☆バニー was already present in DanceDanceRevolution (2013). * ちゅ～いん☆バニー received CHALLENGE charts as part of the ''鬼のEXTRA ATTACK'' (Oni no EXTRA ATTACK) event of DanceDanceRevolution (2014). These charts were unlockable from August 15th, 2014, to September 12th, 2014. ** From July 16th, 2015 to December 16th, 2015, these charts could be unlocked again via EXTRA ATTACK. ** From December 17th, 2015 onwards, these charts have been automatically unlocked for all players. == Song Production Information == === Yasuhiro Abe === The concept was to make "a fantastic anime song"!
I built the melody while thinking about a story in my mind.
I used to watch a lot of old anime frequently and sing a lot, so I was able to create this song while remembering those nostalgic feelings.
The key to this song are the phrases, which are so catchy that you can remember them after just one listen!
I didn't know who to choose as a vocalist for this song.
I had several singers, but then I decided to go with "Miya", a student of mine who was a perfect fit!
Miya's high-tension vocals and lines are a must-listen! === Benio === My first impression when I got the song was that it was a pop song with a nostalgic feel to it.
It had an exciting feeling, like of a child dreaming of adventures and transformations.
About its image, it is something like a fairy tale or Alice in Wonderland.
However, as there is progression on the melody at the end, I thought that it could represent the middle ground between an adult and a child.
What is important is to express the worldview of the song with simple words and without problems, right? That is the point. === Miya === I'm Miya, the main vocalist of this song.
This is a cute and energetic song with lots of dialogue, so I'm sure you'll have fun dancing to it!
Please play it☆

}} == Song Connections / Remixes == * An instrumental version of ミライプリズム, titled ''ミライプリズム(instrumental)'', appears in the [[Mirai prism (album)|ミライプリズム]] album. * A re-arranged version of ミライプリズム credited to ここなつ meets 日向美ビタースイーツ♪, appears in the [[Chocolate Smile Girls!!]] album. ** A game size version of this version, titled '''ミライプリズム(collaboration ver.)''', appears in REFLEC BEAT groovin'!! Upper, jubeat prop, and pop'n music ラピストリア as part of the 怪盗BisCoの予告状!! event. * A remix of ミライプリズム by [[Masaya Oya|かめりあ]], featuring vocals by GUMI and Miku Hatsune, titled ''ミライプリズム(かめりあ's "Refraction of the story" Remix)'', appears in tilt-six's ''Hope Sound'' album. * Another remix of ミライプリズム by [[KARUT]], titled ''ミライプリズム -KARUT Remix-'', appears in ここなつ2.0's [[Romancing escape|ロマンシングエスケープ]] album. == Trivia == {{Gallery}} * ミライプリズム originates from [[HinaBitter|HinaBitter♪]] (ひなビタ♪), a [[Tomosuke Funaki|TOMOSUKE]] and FujimiShobo (富士見書房) media mix project. It's the first HinaBitter♪ song to feature the members of the ''Coconatsu'' (ここなつ) rival unit, Cocona Shinonome and Natsuhi Shinonome. ** Also, ミライプリズム is the first HinaBitter♪ song to appear in the SOUND VOLTEX series. * ミライプリズム was added to SOUND VOLTEX II -infinite infection- on July 4th, 2014. * ミライプリズム was released as a digital single on July 16th, 2014 and was later included in the ミライプリズム album. ** It also appeared later in ここなつ's [[Synchro notes|シンクロノーツ]] album. ** ミライプリズム also marks tilt-six's debut in BEMANI. * ミライプリズム was added to DanceDanceRevolution (2014) on March 12th, 2015, as part of the [[Hinatabi Bitter Sweets & Coconatsu festival!|日向美ビタースイーツ♪＆ここなつフェスティバル!]] (Hinatabi Bitter Sweets♪ & Coconatsu festival!) event. * Due to licensing issues with Sony Music, ミライプリズム is the only KONAMI original song that is absent from the North American/European versions of [[AC DDR A|DanceDanceRevolution A]]. ** It was added later with the release of the North American version of [[AC DDR A20|DanceDanceRevolution A20]]. * The Chocolate Smile Girls!!' booklet only list the Japanese lyrics for ミライプリズム, omitting the English lyrics. * ミライプリズム(collaboration ver.) is one of the unlocks of the [[Kaitou BisCo no yokokujou!!]] (怪盗BisCoの予告状!!) event. It could be unlocked in jubeat prop, pop'n music ラピストリア, and REFLEC BEAT groovin'!! Upper from June 17th to December 21st, 2015, after the ひなビタ♪ Museum is completed. ** Since jubeat Qubell, ミライプリズム(collaboration ver.) is playable by default. ** Since December 22nd, 2015 in [[AC pnm eclale|pop'n music éclale]], ミライプリズム(collaboration ver.) is playable by default. ** In [[AC RB VOLZZA 2|REFLEC BEAT VOLZZA 2]], ミライプリズム(collaboration ver.) could be purchased in the Garage for 20 VOLZZA KEYs. * On the 怪盗BisCoの予告状！！'s website, ミライプリズム(collaboration ver.) was initially mistakenly credited to '''[[OSTER project]]'''. This was changed shortly to '''日向美ビタースイーツ♪ & ここなつ'''. * In pop'n music, if ミライプリズム(collaboration ver.) is played with 東雲夏陽 as your character, 東雲心菜 will be your rival character instead of her. * ミライプリズム was added to jubeat Qubell on June 9th, 2016, as part of the [[Coconatsu birthday|ここなつバースデー]] event. * After being removed from the initial release of [[AC RB Reflesia|REFLEC BEAT 悠久のリフレシア]], ミライプリズム(collaboration ver.) was revived on December 28th, 2017. * ミライプリズム's [[CS jb 2021|jubeat (2021)]] ratings were adjusted to its jubeat clan ratings on March 7th, 2022. * ミライプリズム(collaboration ver.) is absent from the North American release of [[AC pnm High Cheers!!|pop'n music High☆Cheers!!]]. == Music Comment == None. == Song Production Information == Hinatabi Bitter Sweets♪ and Coconatsu have quickly become closer to each other after creating "[[Two man live]]" and "[[Kimochi connect]]" together.

It features a gold colored skin. * "Nageki no ki" (嘆きの樹) can be translated as "Tree of Lamentation". ** It is translated in French as "Arbre triste" in ''嘆きの樹 Arbre triste -a la viennoise-''. * Kinjishi (金獅子) translates to "Golden Lion". * At the time of its release, 嘆きの樹's Single NORMAL chart had the most notes of any Single NORMAL chart in beatmania IIDX, with 902 notes. ** This was topped by G59 in beatmania IIDX 17 SIRIUS, with 906 notes. * 嘆きの樹 is one of the unlockable crossover songs for DanceDanceRevolution (2014) on the [[Hakken! These charts can be unlocked via ''EXTRA ATTACK''. ** 嘆きの樹's CHALLENGE charts are the first charts in the DanceDanceRevolution series to be originally rated Level 18 and not have BPM changes, stops, or Shock Arrows. ** Since July 23rd, 2015, 嘆きの樹 could be unlocked via EXTRA ATTACK, along with its CHALLENGE charts. ** In [[AC DDR A|DanceDanceRevolution A]], it can be unlocked through ''EXTRA SAVIOR''. ** As of [[AC DDR A20|DanceDanceRevolution A20]], it is available by default. * Keeping with the theme of 嘆きの樹's dark undertones, its Single EXPERT and Double CHALLENGE charts in DanceDanceRevolution have a max combo of 666. * 嘆きの樹 was added to [[CS INFINITAS|beatmania IIDX INFINITAS]] on May 2nd, 2018 as part of the May 2018 Basic Subscription Monthly Songs. ** From June 2020, it can be purchased with BITs. * 嘆きの樹 is available in [[CS DDR GRAND PRIX|DanceDanceRevolution GRAND PRIX]]'s GRAND PRIX mode from March 20th, 2023, by purchasing '''GRAND PRIX music pack vol.17''' (グランプリ楽曲パック vol.17). * 嘆きの樹 was released as a [[BEMANI Premium Archive Disc#Second Release|BEMANI Premium Archive Disc]] in March 2024. == Song Production Information == === Kinjishi === Nageki no ki None of my previous songs had such a difficult birth like this one.
No, I'm wrong. It wasn't that it was a difficult birth. I didn't know what kind of song I should create.
I've created many ONE MORE songs so far. I wasn't worried about it until now.
However, this time, this is a king of kings song, which appears after defeating the four kings.
Furthermore, [[Yoshitaka Nishimura|these]] [[Jun Wakita|Four]] [[Ryutaro Nakahara|Heavenly]] [[Tatsuya Shimizu|Kings]] are all recognized as talented people. With all that in mind, what should I create?
Drum'n'bass? Should I go with happy hardcore? Or Baroque mixture? No matter what image it has, it's still just a king. Time merely passed without being connected to the king of kings. Existing styles won't work. It needs to be something unprecedented in the IIDX series. --- Something unprecedented. From those words, I remembered a certain type of music. Atonal music.
Around the 1900s, some musicians who were tired of existing music concepts such as do-re-mi-fa-so-la-ti-do, started studying to create completely new music which fundamentally overturned the existing musical concepts until then. Although this "experiment" received praise from a minority of music fans and continues to exist in various forms, many people's sensibilities made it difficult for them to accept, and it's extremely rare for it to be part of major music scenes.
By the way, there's a theory that minimal techno was developed from one of those techniques, the twelve-tone technique, but I'm going off-topic, so let's discuss this another time. I attempted atonal music from 100 years ago. Isn't this perfect for my current mental state?
Having said that, I just vaguely remember these stories from music class, and I don't have any knowledge of contemporary music. However, I don't have time to learn this now.
Relying on just my own senses, I created a barely unclear and uncomfortable sound. There are no chords or scales that you can think of when creating a normal song, which feels like adding pieces to a jigsaw puzzle. However, the middle section became so difficult to figure out, that I couldn't understand it myself as a maniac, and since it clearly wasn't going to be accepted by many people, I added a Baroque-style development in the middle section, which completely incorporates the essence of video game music.
This is the song that I made, named "Nageki no ki" together with GOLI, and that's how it was born. Come to think of it, this song probably wouldn't have been born if I didn't make a king of kings song.
While I simultaneously had a mysterious sense, I'm grateful to beatmania IIDX for giving me this kind of opportunity. == Video Production Information == === GOLI === That lamentation fuels me. It was quite difficult. These animations might've been the most difficult to create....
A big boss which surpasses the Four Heavenly Kings. This song's contents are simply large in scale, so I needed to make them according to these contents. And I needed them to appear throughout this song for a long time without ruining its atmosphere. This was quite difficult. If it's already like this, even though this abstract image doesn't have a name like God, I thought about trying to pick up mentally ill humans with troubling emotions.
Such related words flow underneath the cabinet's monitor. If you have free time, say them all. They're all just tiring words. These clustered emotions seem to be gathered as evil things in the present day. I tried to layer the animations with a "tree" image. That's spinning round and round in the depths.
Those shapeshifting gods surrounding it... they're the respective Four Heavenly Kings that were already defeated, and they have the image of a spirit revived by the "tree" of "lamentation" surrounding the present day.
I also tried to make "Nageki no ki"'s exclusive frame appear gold to match Kinjishi's name (Golden Lion).
It has the image of useless, disgusting, and ominous debris left behind by greed. The Four Heavenly Kings planned to incorporate fantasy elements in that way, so how was it? I think it was difficult to make in various ways, but good job to all the main staff involved in the Four Heavenly Kings project! == Difficulty & Notecounts == beatmania IIDX difficulty rated from 1 to 12.

To unlock it, you must equip a Q-pro with the following attire, earned in STEP UP from the following months: ** Head: Oni (February) ** Hair: Summer (August) ** Face: any ** Clothes: Hinamatsuri (March) ** Hand: Jiorcho (GOAL) *** Once these are all equipped on your Q-pro, 突撃！ガラスのニーソ姫！ will be unlocked. *** Fittingly, 突撃！ガラスのニーソ姫's overlays involve dress-up as well. * 突撃！ガラスのニーソ姫！ translates to "Assault! The glass knee-socks princess!" ** When 突撃！ガラスのニーソ姫！ is played on beatmania IIDX, the arcade LED marquee displays "RUSH! PRINCESS GLASS OVER-KNEE!". * 突撃！ガラスのニーソ姫！ marks Youhei Kimura's first original composition in BEMANI. ** It also marks Momiji Yamamoto's debut in BEMANI. *** 突撃！ガラスのニーソ姫！ being crossed over also marks her first appearance in the DanceDanceRevolution series. * According to Youhei Kimura, he had to rewrite 突撃！ガラスのニーソ姫！ several times over before it was completed. * 突撃！ガラスのニーソ姫！'s video contains several references to characters from other BEMANI games: ** The princess' mirror has a similar face to pop'n music character Wilhelm from [[Ubertreffen|Übertreffen]] (who was drawn by GOLI, too). His outfit and mask is also shown while trying on outfits. ** When trying on outfits, one of them is the same outfit of pop'n music character TSURARA from [[White Eve]], another GOLI-drawn character. ** beatmania IIDX mascot [[TRAN]]'s hair/clothes also appear twice in the song, too. Once more, she appears as a decorative statue on the post at the bottom of the staircase. ** The princess wears several bands with the face of pop'n music mascot [[Nyami]] on them. * 突撃！ガラスのニーソ姫！ was added to BeatStream on January 15th, 2015. Its MEDIUM and BEAST charts could be unlocked via the Mei mail ''Kotoshi mo yoroshiku'' in ''Takahashi-san Lab.''. ** As of December 3rd, 2015, these charts have been unlocked by default. * 突撃！ガラスのニーソ姫！ uses a unique version of its video from beatmania IIDX in the BeatStream series, eliminating the generic video used between the overlays, making the song only show the overlays and repeating them to cover the length. ** The DanceDanceRevolution series also uses this version of 突撃！ガラスのニーソ姫！'s video, which eliminates any on-screen dancers prior to [[AC DDR WORLD|DanceDanceRevolution WORLD]]. * 突撃！ガラスのニーソ姫！ is one of the unlocks of the [[Kaitou BisCo no yokokujou!!]] (怪盗BisCoの予告状!!) event. It could be unlocked in DanceDanceRevolution (2014) from June 17th to December 21st, 2015, as one of the panel unlocks of the DanceDanceRevolution Museum. ** From January 7th, 2016, 突撃！ガラスのニーソ姫！ can be unlocked in DanceDanceRevolution (2014) via ''EXTRA ATTACK''. ** In [[AC DDR A|DanceDanceRevolution A]], 突撃！ガラスのニーソ姫！ can be unlocked via ''EXTRA SAVIOR''. ** As of [[AC DDR A20|DanceDanceRevolution A20]], it is available by default. * 突撃！ガラスのニーソ姫！'s BEGINNER chart is the second BEGINNER chart to have corner jumps, after [[Over The "Period"|Over The “Period”]]. ** It is also the first non-boss song to have a BEGINNER chart with corner jumps. * 突撃！ガラスのニーソ姫！'s Single/Double DIFFICULT and EXPERT charts were slightly modified in DanceDanceRevolution A on August 30th, 2016. * 突撃！ガラスのニーソ姫！ is unlockable in [[CS INFINITAS|beatmania IIDX INFINITAS]] from August 2nd, 2017, after purchasing its charts with [[CS INFINITAS/BIT unlocks|BITs]]. ** From April 20th, 2022, it is available by default in [[CS INFINITAS 2020|beatmania IIDX INFINITAS (2020)]]. * 突撃！ガラスのニーソ姫！ is available in [[CS DDR GRAND PRIX|DanceDanceRevolution GRAND PRIX]]'s GRAND PRIX mode from March 13th, 2024, by purchasing '''BEMANI SELECTION music pack vol.1''' (BEMANI SELECTION楽曲パック vol.1). == Song Production Information == Untranslated. == Video Production Information == Untranslated. == Difficulty & Notecounts == beatmania IIDX difficulty rated from 1 to 12.

== Song Connections / Remixes == * ÆTHER shares some similarities with [[Cosmic Hurricane]], from the [[Tsugidoka!]] (つぎドカ!) event. * The version of ÆTHER used in the beatmania IIDX, DanceDanceRevolution, and ミライダガッキ series has louder piano sounds in the middle of the song. ** This version of ÆTHER appears in the [[DanceDanceRevolution ORIGINAL SOUNDTRACK VOL.2]] album. * The ending part of ÆTHER utilizes a similar sounding portion of [[PARANOiA Revolution]]'s beat structure, from [[AC DDR X3|DanceDanceRevolution X3 VS 2ndMIX]]. * A vocal version of ÆTHER by [[Masaya Nakamura|Hommarju]], titled ''ÆTHER –Try to Sing Ver.-'', appears in the [[We are "Try to Singers"|We are “Try to Singers”]] album. ** An instrumental version of ÆTHER –Try to Sing Ver.- also appears in We are “Try to Singers”. == Trivia == * ÆTHER is one of the unlockable songs of the second phase of REFLEC BEAT colette -Summer-'s ''Pastel Adventure'' colette Fishing unlocking system. ** From [[AC RB groovin'!!|REFLEC BEAT groovin'!!]] to [[AC RB VOLZZA 2|REFLEC BEAT VOLZZA 2]], ÆTHER was playable by default. * ÆTHER is Yasuhiro Taguchi's first non-DanceDanceRevolution original song under his TAG underground alias. ** It is also Yasuhiro Taguchi's first song in the REFLEC BEAT series with a HARD chart rated Level 10+ (11 or 12 in [[AC RB VOLZZA|REFLEC BEAT VOLZZA]]/VOLZZA 2). * According to ancient and medieval science, æther or ether is the material that fills the region of the universe above the terrestrial sphere. * In REFLEC BEAT, ÆTHER'S BPM halves to 96 in the middle of the song. ** In DanceDanceRevolution, all of ÆTHER'S BPM values are doubled. ** In beatmania IIDX, its LEGGENDARIA also has a brief 24 BPM part near the end of the 96 BPM portion before speeding up to 192 BPM. * ÆTHER was added as a default song to beatmania IIDX 21 SPADA on March 25th, 2014, as part of the [[TAG seitansai]] (TAG生誕祭) event. * ÆTHER is one of DanceDanceRevolution (2013)'s special EXTRA STAGE songs. It was added on March 25th, 2014, as part of the TAG生誕祭 event. ** ÆTHER and [[esrev:eR]] are the first BEMANI crossover songs in the arcade DanceDanceRevolution series that are used as EXTRA STAGE songs. ** In [[AC DDR 2014|DanceDanceRevolution (2014)]], it could be unlocked via the ''EXTRA ATTACK'' unlocking method. ** From December 17th, 2015 onwards, ÆTHER has been automatically unlocked for all players. * From DanceDanceRevolution (2014) onwards, ÆTHER appears in the DanceDanceRevolution (2014) folder instead of the (2013) folder. * In DanceDanceRevolution (2014), before June 17th, 2014, ÆTHER was sorted alphabetically after [[A Stupid Barber]], which meant it was sorted as "ATHER". It is now sorted between [[Adularia]] and [[AFRONOVA]], as "AETHER". * After being removed from the initial release of [[AC RB Reflesia|REFLEC BEAT 悠久のリフレシア]], ÆTHER was revived on December 28th, 2017. * ÆTHER is available in [[CS INFINITAS|beatmania IIDX INFINITAS]] by purchasing '''beatmania IIDX INFINITAS Music Pack vol.6''' (beatmania IIDX INFINITAS 楽曲パック vol.6). * ÆTHER's difficulty level change from [[AC DDR A20|DanceDanceRevolution A20]] was applied to [[AC DDR A|DanceDanceRevolution A]] on March 27th, 2019. * ÆTHER is available in [[CS DDR GRAND PRIX|DanceDanceRevolution GRAND PRIX]]'s GRAND PRIX mode from March 1st, 2022, by purchasing '''GRAND PRIX music pack vol.3''' (グランプリ楽曲パック vol.3). * ÆTHER received LEGGENDARIA charts in [[AC RESIDENT|beatmania IIDX 30 RESIDENT]]'s ARENA MODE. == Song Connections / Remixes == None. == Trivia == * Beautiful Dream marks REDALiCE's debut in the DanceDanceRevolution series. ** It also marks REDALiCE's first appearance in the GuitarFreaks & DrumMania series. ** It also marks Ayumi Nomiya's first appearance in the DanceDanceRevolution, GuitarFreaks & DrumMania, and REFLEC BEAT series. * Beautiful Dream's charts were written by REDALiCE himself. * On the DanceDanceRevolution (2013) location tests, Beautiful Dream had CHALLENGE charts. These charts weren't available for play when the game was released. ** Beautiful Dream's CHALLENGE charts could be unlocked from October 31st, 2013 to November 25th, 2013 by [[KONAMI Arcade Championship|KONAMI Arcade Championship 2013]] players. ** In [[AC DDR 2014|DanceDanceRevolution (2014)]], these charts could be unlocked from October 16th, 2014, to November 13th, 2014 as part of the ''鬼のEXTRA ATTACK'' (Oni no EXTRA ATTACK) event. *** As of July 16th, 2015, these charts can be unlocked again via ''EXTRA ATTACK''. *** From December 17th, 2015 onwards, these charts have been automatically unlocked for all players. * Beautiful Dream was added to GITADORA on August 11th, 2013 as part of the [[jubeat-GITADORA-DDR no Triple Journey|jubeat・GITADORA・DDRのTriple Journey]] unlock event, which started on August 1st, 2013. ** To unlock Beautiful Dream on GITADORA, you must log in the GITADORA official site, go to Play Data, then "music by alphabet", and then order by "な行・は行". At the bottom, click at [[BABY-LON]] (バビロン) to unlock Beautiful Dream. ** From October 1st, 2013, it could be unlocked in GITADORA for 5000 Live Pts. *** In [[AC GD OverDrive|GITADORA OverDrive]], it is available by default for new players with an [[e-amusement|eAMUSEMENT]] PASS. *** As of the end of March 2014 in GITADORA OverDrive, it is available by default for all players. * Beautiful Dream is one of the unlockable songs of the first phase of REFLEC BEAT colette -Autumn-'s ''Pastel Adventure'' colette Harvest unlocking system. ** From [[AC RB groovin'!!|REFLEC BEAT groovin'!!]] to [[AC RB VOLZZA 2|REFLEC BEAT VOLZZA 2]], Beautiful Dream was playable by default. * Beautiful Dream is available in [[CS DDR GRAND PRIX|DanceDanceRevolution GRAND PRIX]]'s GRAND PRIX mode from April 25th, 2022, by purchasing '''GRAND PRIX music pack vol.5''' (グランプリ楽曲パック vol.5). * Beautiful Dream is available in [[CS GD Konasute|コナステ GITADORA]] by purchasing '''Konasute GITADORA HISTORY PACK vol.16''' (コナステ GITADORA HISTORYパック vol.16). == Song Production Information == === REDALiCE === Nice to meet you, DDR players throughout the world! I'm REDALiCE from [[HARDCORE TANO*C]]!!
I'm so honored to have the chance to make a song for DDR!

Other Music Game Appearances: * [[AC DDR 2013|DanceDanceRevolution (2013)]] == Lyrics == None. == Song Connections / Remixes == None. == Trivia == {{Gallery}} * Desert Journey is Takayuki Ishikawa's first DanceDanceRevolution CS original song. * Desert Journey is the only non-boss instrumental KONAMI original song in DanceDanceRevolution HOTTEST PARTY2. * In DanceDanceRevolution HOTTEST PARTY2 / [[CS DDR FuruFuruParty|フルフル♪パーティー]], Desert Journey uses the ''Double Stomp'' and ''Foot Confuser'' gimmicks. * The choreography for Desert Journey would later be recycled for [[0/1 ANGEL]] in [[CS DDR Winx Club|DanceDanceRevolution Winx Club]]. ** Curiously, Desert Journey and 0/1 ANGEL share some similarities: both are 140 BPM and are in the key of C-sharp/D-flat major. * Desert Journey can be unlocked in DanceDanceRevolution (2013) and [[AC DDR 2014|DanceDanceRevolution (2014)]] by reaching ENJOY LEVEL 40. ** From [[AC DDR A|DanceDanceRevolution A]] onwards, Desert Journey is playable by default. * Desert Journey received Double charts in DanceDanceRevolution (2013). ** It also received brand-new CHALLENGE charts in DanceDanceRevolution (2013), which can be unlocked by reaching ENJOY LEVEL 90. *** These charts are unlocked by default from DanceDanceRevolution A onwards. * Desert Journey is available in [[CS DDR GRAND PRIX|DanceDanceRevolution GRAND PRIX]]'s GRAND PRIX mode from June 24th, 2022, by purchasing '''GRAND PRIX music pack vol.7''' (グランプリ楽曲パック vol.7). == Song Production Information == === dj TAKA === A desert town, Las Vegas. It's all about entertainment.
Las Vegas is one of my favorite cities.
The town itself is very modernized and doesn't look like a desert town. But if you look at the city from a plane or Cessna, it looks like floating in the middle of a desert.
I created this song while imagining getting out of the town and driving a 4WD exhilaratingly in the sunbaked desert. Let's drive east, to the next town. === DanceDanceRevolution Community === Take a journey with dj TAKA as he creates a symphonic masterpiece for HOTTEST PARTY2! This song is filled with epic melodies, lush pads, and energetic rhythms. Everything you have come to know and expect from this unique composer. == Difficulty & Notecounts == DanceDanceRevolution difficulty rated from 1 to 10 from DDRMAX2 to SuperNOVA2, and 1 to 20 from X onwards. It could be unlocked in pop'n music High☆Cheers!! from February 26th, 2026 to March 22nd, 2026. * In the pop'n music series, instead of displaying its character's portrait, Monkey Business displays its jacket on the song selection screen. * Monkey Business is available in [[CS INFINITAS 2020|beatmania IIDX INFINITAS (2020)]] by purchasing '''beatmania IIDX INFINITAS The 4th Selection Music Pack vol.1''' (beatmania IIDX INFINITAS The 4th セレクション 楽曲パック vol.1). == Music Comment == None. == Song Production Information == === kors k === Lately, Dubstep has exploded in popularity all over the world, to the point of reaching a state of oversaturation. It's at the point that you'd ask yourself, "Is it alright to make another dubstep track now?" since Trap has been on a boom and taking over. In Monkey Business, I created a song that's Hard Electrik (Hard Dance + Electro) with Trap. It's a sound rapidly gathering an audience, blending Hip Hop, Dubstep, Hard Style, and Juke. Being a fan of trendy music, how could I resist? The title "Monkey Business" (which means "trickery" and "deception") due to the evil gangster image of hip hop as well as the primate-like noises of the synths at the beginning of the track. I think it's a bit more subdued than my works on other series, but DDR gave me the chance to make the music I wanted to at the moment, so I was able to have fun in the creation. The game's sequence data incorporates that stomping dance step found in juke. It might challenge your stamina, but I hope you all enjoy it. In kors k's words: the genre is "Trolling Ook-Ooky!" == Character Information == None. == Difficulty & Notecounts == beatmania IIDX difficulty rated from 1 to 12.

Their modern descendants include the Kazakhs, Kyrgyz, Bashkirs, and Tatars. * Qipchāq was added to REFLEC BEAT colette -Autumn- on October 23rd, 2013 as a default song. * Qipchāq's difficulty level change from [[AC DDR A20|DanceDanceRevolution A20]] was applied to [[AC DDR A|DanceDanceRevolution A]] on March 27th, 2019. * Qipchāq is available in [[CS DDR GRAND PRIX|DanceDanceRevolution GRAND PRIX]]'s GRAND PRIX mode from January 30th, 2023, by purchasing '''GRAND PRIX music pack vol.13''' (グランプリ楽曲パック vol.13). == Song Production Information == === Seiya Murai === For this new DDR song, I brought back my old alias for making fanciful ethnic music "world sequence".
I first discussed this song at the unveiling of the new DDR cabinet at the arcade show earlier this year. Lately I've been receiving more and more requests to do non-pop songs and venture off a little bit into different rhythm songs, so I suppose this song falls into that category?
I was asked to make a song outside the typical dance song, so it was decided that I would make a song inspired by the marching of soldiers and that was combined with a folksy-color to the song to make it sound intercontinental. Qipchaq was the original name given to the region of central Asia by the old tribes who lived there. You may remember reading about this tribe in your history textbook as part of Genghis Khan's Mongolian empire, but it seems that the tribe was filled with brave warriors and the region was often engrossed in battles. I named the song Qipchaq because the song has the image of warriors wondering through the vast grass plains on their horses, although this title was added after the song was composed (laughs). Thanks to the title, I was able to learn a little bit about Chinese history. I think that you can imagine traveling through the vast grass plains while you dance to this song. == Difficulty & Notecounts == DanceDanceRevolution difficulty rated from 1 to 20 from X onwards.

== Song Connections / Remixes == None. == Trivia == {{Gallery}} * Top The Charts received a unique video in DanceDanceRevolution (PS3). This video has never been used in any other DanceDanceRevolution game. * Top The Charts can be unlocked in DanceDanceRevolution (2013) and [[AC DDR 2014|DanceDanceRevolution (2014)]] by reaching ENJOY LEVEL 20. ** From [[AC DDR A|DanceDanceRevolution A]] onwards, Top The Charts is playable by default. * Top The Charts received Double charts in DanceDanceRevolution (2013). ** It also received brand-new CHALLENGE charts in DanceDanceRevolution (2013), which can be unlocked by reaching ENJOY LEVEL 70. *** These charts are unlocked by default from DanceDanceRevolution A onwards. * Jamie's comments were omitted from Top The Charts' song production information in the DanceDanceRevolution (2013) official website, probably due to her mentioning [[Naoki Maeda|NAOKI]]. * Top The Charts is available in [[CS DDR GRAND PRIX|DanceDanceRevolution GRAND PRIX]]'s GRAND PRIX mode from March 20th, 2023, by purchasing '''GRAND PRIX music pack vol.18''' (グランプリ楽曲パック vol.18). * While Top The Charts' jacket in DanceDanceRevolution (PS3) shows the woman wearing a slightly transparent outfit, the Nintendo Wii version of the jacket was censored by making it completely opaque. ** The arcade DanceDanceRevolution games and DanceDanceRevolution GRAND PRIX use the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 version of the jacket, though DanceDanceRevolution (2013)'s official website shows the Nintendo Wii version instead. == Song Production Information == === Jamie === Well I always loved NAOKI and the rest of BEMANI, so I wanted to produce a track that would say "DDR & Retro", something that would bring us back to the beginning of the DDR History. So I modeled it after NAOKI and classic DDR sound. So me and my best friend music partner Dave have teamed up for this, along side our wonderful singer Hanna from the famous group SMiLE.dk! === Dave === This one really feels like a signature song for DDR. With the melody line we composed the female vocalist Hanna, who is from the newest SMiLE.dk album Around the World, truely brings you into the song. When you play this song, you truly feel like you are playing, DDR! === Hanna === When I was writing the lyrics, I wanted it to inspire and hype the players to play better and feel really positive about themselves and get them to "reach for the stars". The other Triple Journey songs are: ** [[Triple Journey -S-C-U EDITION-]], which appears in [[AC jb saucer|jubeat saucer]]. ** [[Triple Journey -OJ EDITION-]], which appears in [[AC GD|GITADORA]]. == Trivia == * Triple Journey -TAG EDITION- was added to DanceDanceRevolution (2013) on August 31st, 2013 as the final song of the [[jubeat-GITADORA-DDR no Triple Journey|jubeat・GITADORA・DDRのTriple Journey]] unlock event. ** To unlock Triple Journey -TAG EDITION- on DanceDanceRevolution, you must have read all of the previous days' mails on the Triple Journey official site, then read the August 31st mail and click on the unlocking button. ** From October 1st, 2013, it could be unlocked in DanceDanceRevolution (2013) and [[AC DDR 2014|DanceDanceRevolution (2014)]] by playing thirteen rounds with an [[e-amusement|eAMUSEMENT]] PASS. ** From [[AC DDR A|DanceDanceRevolution A]] onwards, Triple Journey -TAG EDITION- is playable by default. * The jubeat・GITADORA・DDRのTriple Journey's characters, Smith, OTOBEAR, and [[BABY-LON]], appear in Triple Journey -TAG EDITION-'s jacket. * When sorted alphabetically, Triple Journey -TAG EDITION- was erroneously sorted under the "U" folder in DanceDanceRevolution (2013). As GITADORA was part of the event, it was difficult to think of the direction of the song so that it could be enjoyed in DDR, so we finally decided to do different arrangements for each series.
For the DDR version, I imagined an scene where someone did not finish their homework at all on August 31st, and it is catching up with anger.
I was serious because I was supposed to finish it in July, but if I work hard from September until the first lesson of the new school year, I will be fine. Then I remembered that there are friends with other play styles, such as those who forget the homework at home, and those who never do it. == Difficulty & Notecounts == DanceDanceRevolution difficulty rated from 1 to 20 from X onwards. The name of the ACT 2 boss is ''Vega Rabbit'', which is the only ぼくらの宇宙戦争 character that isn't shown in the ''beatmania IIDX 21 SPADA ORIGINAL SOUNDTRACK'' booklet. ** In [[AC SPADA|beatmania IIDX 21 SPADA]], its NORMAL, HYPER, and ANOTHER charts can be unlocked by obtaining 102, 110, and 118 Tran Medals respectively. ** As of July 24th, 2014, it could be unlocked in beatmania IIDX 21 SPADA and [[AC PENDUAL|22 PENDUAL]] through the [[Hakken! Yomigaetta BEMANI iseki|発見！よみがえったBEMANI遺跡]] event. ** As of July 1st, 2015, it could be purchased in beatmania IIDX 22 PENDUAL with ''Youkou no hologram'' (陽光のホログラム). ** As of [[AC copula|beatmania IIDX 23 copula]], it is available by default. * VEGA is REDALiCE's first purely instrumental song in beatmania IIDX. * According to REDALiCE, VEGA took him three days and nights to complete. ** He also notes he was surprised by the video featuring a "gentleman" instead of something cute, or a girl. Fukutomi WAVE makes note of this in her song comments. * Vega is the brightest star in the constellation Lyra, the fifth brightest star in the night sky and the second brightest star in the northern celestial hemisphere, after Arcturus. (放課後★ダンエボ部！) event, which started on April 24th, 2013. * Wow Wow VENUS was one of the qualifying round songs in the [[KONAMI Arcade Championship|KONAMI Arcade Championship 2013]] for DanceEvolution ARCADE. * Wow Wow VENUS was added to DanceDanceRevolution (2013) on October 23rd, 2013 as a default song. ** Like [[Windy Fairy]] and [[printemps]], it displayed its BPM as 96-192 upon its debut. == Song Connections / Remixes == None. == Trivia == {{Gallery}} * からふるぱすてる is ki☆ki's first song as a lead vocalist in the GuitarFreaks & DrumMania series. She previously provided backup vocals for Ayaka in [[Ru-Ru-Ru]]. ** It also marks ki☆ki's first appearance in the DanceDanceRevolution series. * からふるぱすてる is available for play in GuitarFreaksXG & DrumManiaXG as an unlockable song in JukeBox #1 (March 10th, 2010). ** As of April 23rd, 2010, it has been automatically unlocked into Standard Mode. * からふるぱすてる was added to DanceDanceRevolution on August 13th, 2013 as part of the [[jubeat-GITADORA-DDR no Triple Journey|jubeat・GITADORA・DDRのTriple Journey]] unlock event, which started on August 1st, 2013. ** To unlock からふるぱすてる on DanceDanceRevolution, click on the NEW icon (with the shape of OTOBEAR) on the DanceDanceRevolution eAMUSEMENT GATE page. ** From October 1st, 2013, it could be unlocked in DanceDanceRevolution (2013) and [[AC DDR 2014|DanceDanceRevolution (2014)]] by playing six rounds with an [[e-amusement|eAMUSEMENT]] PASS. ** From [[AC DDR A|DanceDanceRevolution A]] onwards, からふるぱすてる is playable by default. * からふるぱすてる's GuitarFreaks & DrumMania video is featured in DanceDanceRevolution. However, it plays in the background of the BIG SCREEN background dance stage and is not full-screen. * からふるぱすてる received a widescreen video in [[AC GD OverDrive|GITADORA OverDrive]] on July 23rd, 2014. This video is a high definition remake of its original video. ** The same video was also added to the DanceDanceRevolution series in DanceDanceRevolution A. Like with the previous video, it is still displayed in the background of the BIG SCREEN stage and is not full-screen prior to [[AC DDR WORLD|DanceDanceRevolution WORLD]]. * One of the girls from からふるぱすてる's video, Kokone (心音), would later become a selectable character in GITADORA OverDrive's Battle System. ** Kokone, alongside Hina (陽夏) and Ryou (涼), would also later become a selectable character in [[AC GD FUZZ-UP|GITADORA FUZZ-UP]]'s ''Daishuugou atsumare together! GITADORA All Star GIG!'' (大集合あつまれトゥギャザー！GITADORAオールスターGIG！) event. * からふるぱすてる's difficulty level change from [[AC DDR A20|DanceDanceRevolution A20]] was applied to DanceDanceRevolution A on March 27th, 2019. * からふるぱすてる (CLASSIC) could be unlocked in [[AC GD EXCHAIN|GITADORA EXCHAIN]] as one of the ''GF&DM CHRONICLE'' 2007～2009 songs from June 5th, 2019, by playing three credits. ** In [[AC GD NEX+AGE|GITADORA NEX+AGE]], it could be unlocked from March 4th to June 21st, 2020 and from October 28th to November 29th, 2020 as part of the ''Thank you! GITADORA 21st kanshasai'' (サンキュー! ギタドラ21st感謝祭) event. ** As of [[AC GD FUZZ-UP|GITADORA FUZZ-UP]], it is available by default. * からふるぱすてる is available in [[CS DDR GRAND PRIX|DanceDanceRevolution GRAND PRIX]]'s GRAND PRIX mode from April 25th, 2022, by purchasing '''GRAND PRIX music pack vol.5''' (グランプリ楽曲パック vol.5). * In DanceDanceRevolution GRAND PRIX, からふるぱすてる received its difficulty change from DanceDanceRevolution WORLD on July 3rd, 2024. == Song Production Information == === Jin Senbonmatsu === ...... I can't guarantee if the song is serious or not, but... This song was a lot of fun to record!
If the song is nonsensical, the recording and editing was also nonsensical.
Every time I had a meeting with ki☆ki, the entire song would change (laughs).
Where are you going? Colorful pastel!? I thought that this kind of thing is one of the best parts of music! And this story is my digression, but...

BEMANIちくわまつり2023]] event. == Trivia == {{Gallery}} * めうめうぺったんたん！！ originates from [[HinaBitter|HinaBitter♪]] (ひなビタ♪), a [[Tomosuke Funaki|TOMOSUKE]] and FujimiShobo (富士見書房) media mix project. It features Meu Meu (芽兎 めう), from the ''Hinatabi Bitter Sweets♪'' (日向美ビタースイーツ♪) unit. Her nickname is "Meumeu" (めうめう). * めうめうぺったんたん！！ was released as a digital single on March 13th, 2013 and was later included on the ひなビタ♪ ORIGINAL SOUNDTRACK album. * めうめうぺったんたん！！ is one of the LIVE unlocks from GITADORA. It was added on April 24th, 2013. ** In [[AC GD OverDrive|GITADORA OverDrive]], it is available by default for new players with an [[e-amusement|eAMUSEMENT]] PASS. ** As of the end of March 2014 in GITADORA OverDrive, it is available by default for all players. * めうめうぺったんたん！！ was added to jubeat saucer on May 1st, 2013. * めうめうぺったんたん！！'s jubeat charts were created by RAG [https://p.eagate.573.jp/game/bemani/fansite/p/report/2014w/report12.html?page=8]. * めうめうぺったんたん！！ was added to pop'n music Sunny Park on May 15th, 2013. * With 1530 notes, めうめうぺったんたん！！'s EX chart holds the record with the highest notecount for a Level 46 chart in pop'n music. * めうめうぺったんたん！！ marks Youhei Kimura's debut on the DanceDanceRevolution, GuitarFreaks & DrumMania, pop'n music, and REFLEC BEAT series. * めうめうぺったんたん！！ was one of the qualifying round songs in the [[KONAMI Arcade Championship|KONAMI Arcade Championship 2013]] for GITADORA DrumMania. * On the iTunes page for めうめうぺったんたん！！, the song's title and artist were changed to '''meumeupeltutantan!!''' and '''Hinatabi Bitter Suites♪''', respectively. * めうめうぺったんたん！！ received a SPECIAL chart in REFLEC BEAT groovin'!! on August 28th, 2014. It could be purchased at the REFLEC Shop for 1200 Refle, after clearing the chart in the FINAL ROUND of the HinaBitter♪ Test (ひなビタ♪検定) added on the same day. ** With 844 Objects, めうめうぺったんたん！！'s SPECIAL chart had the highest notecount of any pre-REFLEC BEAT 悠久のリフレシア chart rated Level 10. ** From October 30th, 2014, it could be purchased without prerequisites. ** In [[AC RB VOLZZA|REFLEC BEAT VOLZZA]], it could be purchased from the Garage for 8 VOLZZA KEYs. ** In [[AC RB VOLZZA 2|REFLEC BEAT VOLZZA 2]], it could be unlocked by clearing its HARD chart a specific number of times, depending on the grade obtained on it (AAA+: 1 time, AAA: 2 times, AA: 3 times, A or lower: 5 times). * めうめうぺったんたん！！ was added to BeatStream on October 9th, 2014. Its MEDIUM and BEAST charts could be unlocked via the BisCo mail ''Stamp pettantan!(*｀ω´*)'' in ''Takahashi-san Lab.''. ** As of December 3rd, 2015, these charts have been unlocked by default. * As of March 12th, 2015, [[AC DDR 2014|DanceDanceRevolution (2014)]] uses BeatStream's unique video for めうめうぺったんたん！！. }} == Song Connections / Remixes == * The full version of dreaming can make a wish come true can be found in the Premium Pack of the PlayStation 3 version of DanceDanceRevolution (2010). == Trivia == {{Gallery}} * dreaming can make a wish come true marks the first and only collaboration between Junko Karashima and Hiroyoshi Kato in BEMANI. * dreaming can make a wish come true was one of the playable songs at the dance-off minigame in the KONAMI Penthouse, a virtual space in PlayStation 3's ''PlayStation Home''. ** In the minigame, the song title was capitalized as '''Dreaming Can Make a Wish Come True'''. * In the DanceDanceRevolution master song list, dreaming can make a wish come true is listed between the songs from [[CS DDR HOTTEST PARTY3|DanceDanceRevolution HOTTEST PARTY3]] / [[CS DDR X2|DanceDanceRevolution X2 CS]], suggesting it was meant to appear in those games first. * dreaming can make a wish come true received Double charts in DanceDanceRevolution X3 VS 2ndMIX. * dreaming can make a wish come true received a unique overlay in DanceDanceRevolution (PS3). * While dreaming can make a wish come true's jacket on the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 versions of DanceDanceRevolution (2010) shows the woman naked, the Nintendo Wii version of the jacket was censored by putting clothes on the woman. ** The arcade DanceDanceRevolution games use the PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 version of the jacket. * dreaming can make a wish come true is available in [[CS DDR GRAND PRIX|DanceDanceRevolution GRAND PRIX]]'s GRAND PRIX mode from May 25th, 2023, by purchasing '''GRAND PRIX music pack vol.22''' (グランプリ楽曲パック vol.22). == Song Production Information == === jun === One day, I really wanted to make a cute and pop song so I wrote this with that thought.
In the DDR series, we have recorded many happy hardcore songs such as [[KIMONO PRINCESS|KIMONO♥PRINCESS]] and [[Sweet Sweet Love Magic|Sweet Sweet ♥ Magic]], but I aimed to write a song that was a little different from these. This time, I asked NRG Factory to arrange this song (it is an official remix), and it was just as I imagined... actually, it exceeded my expectations and I was moved and admired how they expressed my thoughts. Also, Anna's voice was very cute and she helped to fully portray the vibe of this song. Everyone, thank you so much for giving life to this song! I'll be glad if people can enjoy dancing to the atmosphere of this song. == Difficulty & Notecounts == DanceDanceRevolution difficulty rated from 1 to 10 from DDRMAX2 to SuperNOVA2, and 1 to 20 from X onwards. == Song Connections / Remixes == * A slightly rearranged long version of Fever, titled ''Fever -2012 Extended Mix-'', appears on Sota Fujimori's fourth album, [[SYNTHESIZED4]]. == Trivia == * Fever is available in [[CS DDR GRAND PRIX|DanceDanceRevolution GRAND PRIX]]'s GRAND PRIX mode from March 13th, 2024, by purchasing '''BEMANI SELECTION music pack vol.1''' (BEMANI SELECTION楽曲パック vol.1). * In DanceDanceRevolution GRAND PRIX, Fever received its difficulty change from [[AC DDR WORLD|DanceDanceRevolution WORLD]] on July 3rd, 2024. == Song Production Information == === Sota Fujimori === Hello everyone, it's been a while. Recently, I've been providing tracks for various rhythm games, but for the past few years, I've really wanted to make house music.
Ever since I produced songs like [[Do It Right]] and [[Kind Lady]] in the past, I had made up my mind: if I'm going to do house, it has to be for DDR!!
So, when I received this request, I took on the challenge of producing the soulful house track I've always wanted to create.

The ANOTHER "11" is also a good job. I'm happy that this song was included in IIDX. The next game is DanceEvolution... maybe. === jubeat and REFLEC BEAT === Untranslated. === pop'n music === ==== [[Daichi Watanabe|PON]] ==== Everybody, today is a nice day for comments.
Every day is colder than before, how are you feeling?
Please be careful not to catch a cold. Well, "TRANCE CORE / FLOWER" is one of the link event unlockable songs of the pop'n music Sunny Park location test. The location test times of pop'n and REFLEC were close, so we prepared something like a celebration.
The theme of pop'n music Sunny Park is "park", and since the visual effect of the unlocking system at the location test was a flower blossoming with the number of plays, this song stood first and foremost.
Such a popular track which was crossed over to various BEMANI games, will it have a considerable impact once it's unlocked?
I'm glad I was able to add flowers to fantasia and Sunny Park alongside "TWINKLE POP / [[Twinkle Wonderland]]". In summary, PON made this comment instead of DJ YOSHITAKA, who was busy.
I feel nervous when I give comments to someone else's music.
I feel tense and serious as I can only say ordinary things. I love! pop'n music. === Tenkaichi otogesai Zenkoku issei nintei taikai === ==== DJ YOSHITAKA ==== In 2011, I planted a seed.
How much time would it take, how much energy would be needed to sprout it? What would be the color of its flower? What about its shape? How many petals...
Thinking about these problems, I planted it in a land called jubeat.
This seed germinated and "FLOWER" grew to be one of the most famous songs in the BEMANI series.
Now you can play it in every arcade game of the BEMANI series.
Anyways, please appreciate the flowers that are blooming this time with various colors and shapes.
And don't be afraid to touch them.
There are many things that can be challenging, just as you don't know what kind of flower will bloom simply by looking at its seed. == Video Production Information == === Motion Combat === I'm Motion Combat, who was in charge of creating this video.
I'm honored to be in charge of the super masterpiece "Flower". I loudly listened to this song while making the video, which felt really nice★ This video was edited from a DJ YOSHITAKA live video, so you can see him DJ while playing it... it'd be great if you can feel how sound, video, and player are fully synchronized! == Character Information == None. == Choreography Information == === Yuu Kimoto === A seed which came from a different dimension. It enters a body and starts to emit light, create undulating beats from a heartbeat, then freely releases energy in various forms. I created this choreography with such image. When I first listened to this song, I was flustered by the high-speed beat, but I captured "FLOWER"'s power and elegance, and gave it a shape. It's a particularly pleasurable feeling when you can match each location! By all means, please experience it☆ == Staff Comments == === jubeat === ==== T_da ==== DJ YOSHITAKA unreasonably asked me to "draw a jacket design which contains the spirit of a single story", so I thought about the story in detail and selfishly completed it on my own. }} == Song Connections / Remixes == * The full version of Let's Get Away can be found in the Premium Pack of the PlayStation 3 version of DanceDanceRevolution (2010). ** The full version is used as the staff roll song for both the PlayStation 3 and Nintendo Wii versions of that game. * A portion of Let's Get Away is featured in [[CS DDR II|DanceDanceRevolution II]]'s [[DanceDanceRevolution (nonstop megamix)|DanceDanceRevolution]] nonstop megamix. == Trivia == * Let's Get Away was used as the main theme song for DanceDanceRevolution (2010). * The full version of Let's Get Away was performed live in the release event for DanceDanceRevolution (PS3). * Let's Get Away was one of the playable songs at the dance-off minigame in the KONAMI Penthouse, a virtual space in PlayStation 3's ''PlayStation Home''. * In the DanceDanceRevolution master song list, Let's Get Away is listed between the songs from [[CS DDR HOTTEST PARTY3|DanceDanceRevolution HOTTEST PARTY3]] / [[CS DDR X2|DanceDanceRevolution X2 CS]], suggesting it was meant to appear in those games first. * Let's Get Away mistakenly uses its full version's jacket in the Wii version of DanceDanceRevolution (2010), despite the full version not being playable on that game. * An early chart file for Let's Get Away can be found unused within the DanceDanceRevolution (2010) data. Its Single BEGINNER and BASIC charts, as well as both Wii Balance Board charts, are different. * Let's Get Away received a unique video in DanceDanceRevolution (PS3). This video has never been used in any other DanceDanceRevolution game. ** Naoki Maeda appears in Let's Get Away's background video. * Let's Get Away received Double charts in DanceDanceRevolution X3 VS 2ndMIX. * Let's Get Away is available in [[CS DDR GRAND PRIX|DanceDanceRevolution GRAND PRIX]]'s GRAND PRIX mode from June 24th, 2022, by purchasing '''GRAND PRIX music pack vol.7''' (グランプリ楽曲パック vol.7). == Song Production Information == === NAOKI MAEDA === Catchy melodies, a beat that naturally gets your body moving, and beautifully resonant chords...
"Let's Get Away" is a track that perfectly expresses the base elements I always focus on when producing music.
It's the culmination of my musical style over the past few years, and I consider it a major turning point. From this song onward, I plan to challenge myself with new approaches to sound production. I hope you can feel where I'm right "now" through "Let's Get Away". == Difficulty & Notecounts == DanceDanceRevolution difficulty rated from 1 to 10 from DDRMAX2 to SuperNOVA2, and 1 to 20 from X onwards.
